title: Employment & Work Injury
intro: Employment and work injury in India: wages, leave, retrenchment, occupational safety and statutory benefits.

tips.title: Overtime in India: check the Factories Act or your state Shops Act
tips.cost: No direct cost. Keep attendance records, shift rosters and written overtime approvals; a notebook or phone photo is enough.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no single 1.5x, 2x and 3x overtime ladder. Under the Factories Act, 1948, a covered worker who works beyond 9 hours in a day or 48 hours in a week is entitled to twice the ordinary rate. State Shops and Establishments Acts set their own daily and weekly limits and rates. The Code on Wages, 2019 also provides overtime at twice the rate where it applies, but commencement and state rules matter. Check your coverage, keep records, and raise unpaid overtime with the labour commissioner.
tips.benefit: The Factories Act caps ordinary work at 9 hours a day and 48 hours a week and requires double pay for overtime. Many state Shops Acts use a shorter week and a different rate. The Code on Wages sets double pay for overtime where it applies. The exact entitlement depends on the establishment, your role and the state.
tips.sources: Factories Act, 1948 (sections 51, 54, 59). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/1775>; Code on Wages, 2019. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Ministry of Labour and Employment. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Coverage is the hard part. Managerial and supervisory staff may be outside the Factories Act, and small shops may be outside the Shops Act. Do not assume a 1.5x or 3x rate from another country. Ask the labour department which statute covers your workplace.

tips.title: Annual leave in India is set by the Factories Act or your state Shops Act
tips.cost: No cost. Keep leave records and your appointment letter.
tips.inPlainWords: Under the Factories Act, a covered worker gets one day of paid annual leave for every 20 days worked, roughly 15 days a year. State Shops and Establishments Acts set different totals, often 12 to 21 days. There is no national rule that gives 5, 10 or 15 days by total years of service, and no automatic 300% cash payment for unused leave. Carry-forward, encashment and payment on exit depend on the statute and your contract.
tips.benefit: The Factories Act, 1948 (section 79) and state Shops Acts create the leave entitlement. The Code on Social Security and state rules do not create a single national leave table. Check your leave balance, the leave year and the carry-forward rule.
tips.sources: Factories Act, 1948 (section 79). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/1775>; State Shops and Establishments Acts; Ministry of Labour and Employment. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Coverage and carry-forward limits differ. Encashment is not automatic; it depends on the statute, contract or employer policy. Get the leave policy in writing.

tips.title: There is no fixed national probation ladder in India — read the contract and standing orders
tips.cost: No cost. Read the offer letter and standing orders before signing.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not set a general one, two or six month probation limit by contract length. Probation is a contractual term, and for covered establishments the Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946 or state Shops rules may govern confirmation and termination. Probation pay cannot fall below the applicable minimum wage, but the 80% rule is not Indian law. Check the appointment letter for the probation length, notice, confirmation test and extension clause.
tips.benefit: The Standing Orders Act, state Shops Acts and the Code on Industrial Relations, 2020 set procedures for covered establishments. A probation clause that is unfair or vague may be challenged, but there is no statutory maximum for every job.
tips.sources: Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946. <https://labour.gov.in/>; Code on Industrial Relations, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; State Shops and Establishments Acts.
tips.caveats: Coverage depends on the establishment and state. Do not accept a second probation after confirmation without written advice. Keep the letter and any extension.

tips.title: Retrenchment compensation in India is 15 days average pay per completed year, not one month per year
tips.cost: No cost. Use your last 12 months wages and service record.
tips.inPlainWords: For a retrenchment covered by the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, an eligible workman gets 15 days average pay for each completed year of continuous service, plus notice or pay in lieu. The Code on Industrial Relations, 2020 keeps the 15-day formula for retrenchment but changes procedure and thresholds. Gratuity is separate: under the Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972 it is payable after five years of continuous service, at 15 days wages per year.
tips.benefit: The Industrial Disputes Act (section 25F), the Industrial Relations Code and the Payment of Gratuity Act provide the formulas. The retrenchment formula is 15 days, not 30, and eligibility and caps differ.
tips.sources: Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (section 25F). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Code on Industrial Relations, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Not every employee is a workman under the Industrial Disputes Act; managerial staff may rely on contract or civil law. Retrenchment procedure, notice and government permission depend on establishment size and state.

tips.title: Notice pay in India depends on your contract or the governing labour law — there is no automatic N+1
tips.cost: No cost. Read the notice clause and keep the termination letter.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no universal N+1 rule. The notice period is usually in the appointment letter or standing orders. For retrenchment under the Industrial Disputes Act, the employer must give notice or pay in lieu as part of section 25F. State Shops Acts and the Industrial Relations Code set different procedures. Check what your contract says, and get any waiver or payment in lieu in writing.
tips.benefit: The Industrial Disputes Act, the Industrial Relations Code and state Shops Acts provide the procedure. Payment in lieu may be contractual; it is not a statutory one-month add-on in every case.
tips.sources: Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 (section 25F). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Code on Industrial Relations, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; State Shops and Establishments Acts.
tips.caveats: Contracts can be challenged if the notice clause is unfair, but litigation takes time. Do not sign a full and final settlement before checking dues.

tips.title: Challenge a wrongful termination at the labour court or industrial tribunal — India has no fixed 2N formula
tips.cost: Time and legal fees; free legal aid may be available through NALSA.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian law does not give an automatic 2N payment for every unlawful termination. A workman can raise an industrial dispute; the labour court or industrial tribunal may order reinstatement, back wages or compensation. Managerial employees may need a civil suit or arbitration under the contract. Limitation periods and forums depend on the statute and state. Get legal advice before accepting a settlement.
tips.benefit: The Industrial Disputes Act, the Industrial Relations Code and NALSA legal aid provide the routes. Remedies are fact-specific and can include reinstatement or compensation, not a fixed multiplier.
tips.sources: Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Code on Industrial Relations, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; NALSA legal aid. <https://nalsa.gov.in/legal-aid/>
tips.caveats: Delay can bar a claim. The employer may argue misconduct or redundancy. Preserve the termination letter, emails and performance records.

tips.title: Do not sign a resignation you do not mean — it can affect notice, gratuity and your record
tips.cost: No cost; keep copies of everything you sign.
tips.inPlainWords: In India, resignation is usually governed by the contract and state Shops rules. Signing a resignation can affect notice pay, full and final settlement and how the exit is recorded. Gratuity after five years and your EPF balance are statutory and should not be forfeited by a resignation, but other dues may be. Ask for the calculation in writing and do not sign under pressure.
tips.benefit: The Payment of Gratuity Act, the EPF Act and state Shops Acts govern the main entitlements. Resignation is different from retrenchment and from a termination for misconduct.
tips.sources: Payment of Gratuity Act, 1972. <https://labour.gov.in/>; Employees Provident Fund and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; State Shops and Establishments Acts.
tips.caveats: Some employers make settlement conditional on a resignation letter. Get advice before signing if dues are disputed.

tips.title: Save your employment records before you hand back the laptop
tips.cost: About half an hour; no cost.
tips.inPlainWords: Before you leave, save your appointment letter, pay slips, attendance, leave records, PF and ESIC statements and written communications. You will need them to prove wages, notice and contributions. Do not take source code, client lists or confidential documents; that can create a separate dispute.
tips.benefit: Good records make an EPFO or ESIC complaint or a labour claim possible. The employer may restrict access after exit.
tips.sources: Author experience; EPFO employee portal. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Keep only your own employment records. Do not copy trade secrets or client data.

tips.title: Before a dusty, noisy or chemical job, ask for the hazard disclosure and medical checks
tips.cost: No cost; ask before you sign.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian occupational safety law requires employers to identify hazards, provide protective equipment and arrange medical examinations in covered factories and establishments. The Factories Act and the Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020 set duties, but the exact exams and frequency depend on the process and state rules. Ask for the hazard information in writing and keep your medical reports.
tips.benefit: The Factories Act, the OSH Code and state factory rules require hazard controls and medical checks in many hazardous processes.
tips.sources: Factories Act, 1948. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/1775>; Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>
tips.caveats: Coverage varies by establishment and process. A generic medical check is not enough; ask what is tested and who pays.

tips.title: Dust, noise and chemicals can cause permanent damage — use the right protection and refuse unsafe work
tips.cost: Employer-provided equipment; keep your own records.
tips.inPlainWords: Silicosis, noise-induced hearing loss and chemical injuries can be permanent. Covered employers must provide effective protective equipment and safe systems of work; workers can report unsafe conditions to the factory inspector. Retaliation for raising a safety complaint is not lawful. Use equipment that fits and is rated for the hazard, not a cloth mask for fine dust.
tips.benefit: The Factories Act, the OSH Code and ESIC cover prevention and occupational disease. Prevention is the only reliable protection for many conditions.
tips.sources: Factories Act, 1948. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/1775>; Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Code, 2020. <https://labour.gov.in/labour-codes>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Report symptoms early. Keep the hazard assessment and medical reports. A respirator needs fit testing to work.

tips.title: Report a workplace injury at once and start the ESIC or Employees Compensation claim
tips.cost: No cost; keep medical records and witness details.
tips.inPlainWords: Report the injury to your employer immediately and get medical treatment. If you are covered by ESIC, the employer should help with the accident report and the ESIC claim. If not, the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 may make the employer liable. Commuting injuries can be covered in some ESIC cases, but the facts matter. Do not sign a settlement before the medical position is clear.
tips.benefit: The ESIC Act and the Employees Compensation Act provide treatment, cash compensation and dependants benefits in covered cases.
tips.sources: Employees State Insurance Act, 1948. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Employees Compensation Act, 1923. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/19236>
tips.caveats: Coverage depends on insurable employment and contributions. Contractor and principal-employer liability can be complex.

tips.title: If you feel acutely unwell at work, call 112 or 108 first — do not delay for a compensation theory
tips.cost: No cost.
tips.inPlainWords: There is no Indian rule that requires you to wait 48 hours or stay at work to qualify for compensation. If you have chest pain, stroke signs, severe bleeding or breathing trouble, get emergency help immediately. Report the episode to your employer and keep the medical records; any ESIC or compensation claim can be sorted out after you are safe.
tips.benefit: Emergency care first. 112 is the all-in-one emergency number; 108 is the ambulance service in most states. ESIC and the Employees Compensation Act may apply later.
tips.sources: Emergency Response Support System. <https://112.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Do not drive yourself if you are seriously unwell. Ask a colleague to call and stay with you.

tips.title: An uninsured employer is still liable for a work injury
tips.cost: Time and legal help; free legal aid may be available.
tips.inPlainWords: If your employer did not insure you under ESIC, that does not erase the claim. The Employees Compensation Act can make the employer liable, and principal employers can be liable for contractor workers in some cases. Keep proof of employment, wages and the accident. A no-insurance, no-compensation statement is not a legal defence.
tips.benefit: The Employees Compensation Act, ESIC and the Contract Labour Act can create liability. The employer may have to pay from its own funds.
tips.sources: Employees Compensation Act, 1923. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/19236>; Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970. <https://labour.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Proving employment and the accident is the key. Get witness details and medical records early.

tips.title: Disability assessment and compensation follow ESIC or Employees Compensation schedules, not a fixed grade table
tips.cost: Time; no direct fee for the statutory process.
tips.inPlainWords: After a work injury stabilises, ESIC or the Employees Compensation Act provides for medical assessment and disability benefit. The percentage of disability and the compensation depend on the statute and the medical board. Do not sign a one-time settlement before the assessment; get a copy of the report and ask how the figure was calculated.
tips.benefit: ESIC and the Employees Compensation Act provide periodic payments or a lump sum depending on the scheme.
tips.sources: ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Employees Compensation Act, 1923. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/19236>
tips.caveats: Appeals and second opinions may be possible. A private doctors estimate is not the statutory assessment.

tips.title: Work-related death benefits in India come from ESIC or the Employees Compensation Act, not a fixed multiple of income
tips.cost: Administrative time; legal aid may be free.
tips.inPlainWords: If a worker dies from a work injury, dependants may claim ESIC benefits or compensation under the Employees Compensation Act. The amounts depend on wages, the scheme and the dependants. EPF and gratuity may also be payable. Report the death, keep the medical and employment records, and get help from a union or legal-aid lawyer.
tips.benefit: ESIC, the Employees Compensation Act, EPF and the Payment of Gratuity Act can provide benefits to dependants.
tips.sources: ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Employees Compensation Act, 1923. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/19236>; EPFO. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Dependants must prove relationship and dependency. Time limits apply.

tips.title: Document workplace bullying and use the POSH or internal grievance route where it applies
tips.cost: Time; legal help may be needed.
tips.inPlainWords: Sexual harassment at work is covered by the POSH Act, 2013, which requires an internal committee in covered workplaces. General bullying or verbal abuse may be misconduct under standing orders or the contract, but India has no single anti-bullying statute for all workplaces. Record dates, witnesses and messages; use the internal committee, HR or labour authority. Retaliation can strengthen the case.
tips.benefit: The POSH Act, standing orders and research on workplace bullying and health provide the routes. The health risk is real, but the legal route depends on the conduct.
tips.sources: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013. <https://wcd.nic.in/act/sexual-harassment-women-workplace-prevention-prohibition-and-redressal-act-2013>; Xu T et al. (2019). Workplace bullying and cardiovascular disease. <https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2015.302855>
tips.caveats: POSH covers sexual harassment, not every form of bullying. Do not wait if your safety is at risk.

tips.title: Ask for a relieving letter and service certificate when you leave
tips.cost: No cost.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian statutes do not give every employee a single 15-day file-transfer right, but your contract, standing orders or state Shops rules may require an experience or relieving letter. Ask in writing before your last day and keep a copy. PF and ESIC records are separate and should be updated.
tips.benefit: State Shops Acts, standing orders and EPFO/ESIC records support the exit. A service certificate helps the next employer.
tips.sources: State Shops and Establishments Acts; EPFO. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: There is no universal statutory form. If the employer refuses, a written request and labour complaint may help.

tips.title: Check the income-tax treatment of your severance before you spend it
tips.cost: A chartered accountant fee, or free portal guidance.
tips.inPlainWords: India does not exempt severance up to three times the average wage. Retrenchment compensation has a limited exemption under section 10(10B) of the Income Tax Act, subject to the prescribed limit; gratuity, leave encashment and VRS have separate rules. Relief under section 89 may apply. Ask a chartered accountant or use the income-tax portal before assuming the whole amount is tax-free.
tips.benefit: The Income Tax Act sections 10(10B), 10(10C), 10(10AA) and 89, and the Income Tax Department portal, set the treatment.
tips.sources: Income Tax Department. <https://www.incometax.gov.in/>; Income Tax Act, 1961.
tips.caveats: Limits and conditions change. Do not rely on an employers withholding as final.

tips.title: Keep your EPF and ESIC records portable when you change states
tips.cost: No cost; online transfer.
tips.inPlainWords: Your EPF account follows you through your UAN; transfer it when you change jobs instead of withdrawing. ESIC records are linked to your insured person number and can be used across states. Update your nominee and keep your passbook and contribution history. There is no household-registration barrier to these transfers.
tips.benefit: EPFO and ESIC portability keeps your contribution history continuous and helps at retirement and at a claim.
tips.sources: EPFO. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Employer compliance varies. Check your passbook after each job change.

tips.title: Get a written offer letter and employment contract — India has no double-wage penalty for a missing one
tips.cost: No cost.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian law does not impose the double-wages-after-one-month rule for a missing written contract. But a written appointment letter is still essential to prove wages, notice, probation and duties. Covered establishments may have standing orders; state Shops Acts require certain records. If the employer refuses to give a contract, keep emails, payslips and attendance.
tips.benefit: The Contract Act, state Shops Acts and standing orders make written terms important. Written terms reduce disputes.
tips.sources: Indian Contract Act, 1872. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; State Shops and Establishments Acts; Industrial Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 1946.
tips.caveats: Oral contracts can be enforceable but are harder to prove. Do not refuse to sign a contract you have accepted without advice.

tips.title: If EPF or ESIC contributions are missing, complain to EPFO or ESIC and keep your wage records
tips.cost: No cost; time.
tips.inPlainWords: Check your EPF passbook and ESIC contribution history. If contributions are missing or underpaid, raise a grievance with EPFO or ESIC and keep payslips, bank statements and appointment letters. A resignation over the employers statutory breach may affect your notice and dues, so get advice before you resign. A voluntary waiver of PF or ESIC is not a lawful substitute for contributions.
tips.benefit: The EPF Act, the ESIC Act and the EPFO/ESIC grievance portals provide the route.
tips.sources: EPFO. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Contractor and principal-employer responsibility can be shared. Time limits apply.

tips.title: Penalty clauses on resignation are enforceable only to a reasonable extent in India
tips.cost: Legal advice.
tips.inPlainWords: Indian courts do not enforce every penalty clause. Under section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, a court may award reasonable compensation for breach, not the full penalty. A training bond or notice-period recovery may be enforceable if it is reasonable and reflects actual loss. Post-employment non-compete clauses are often hard to enforce. Get the clause reviewed before you pay.
tips.benefit: The Indian Contract Act section 74 and case law require the court to look at reasonableness and actual loss.
tips.sources: Indian Contract Act, 1872 (section 74). <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>
tips.caveats: No fixed formula. A clause that is a penalty, not a genuine pre-estimate, may be reduced.

tips.title: Object in writing to a demotion or salary cut — do not wait and hope it reverses
tips.cost: No cost; legal help may be needed.
tips.inPlainWords: A unilateral demotion or salary cut can be a breach of your contract or standing orders. Write to the employer immediately, state that you do not accept the change, and keep working under protest if you need the income. Indian law has no one-month rule that automatically makes the change valid, but continuing without objection can weaken your case. Get legal advice.
tips.benefit: The Contract Act, the Industrial Disputes Act and state Shops Acts support a prompt written objection and preserve the dispute.
tips.sources: Indian Contract Act, 1872. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Industrial Disputes Act, 1947. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; State Shops and Establishments Acts.
tips.caveats: The outcome depends on the contract and the employers power to transfer or redeploy. Do not resign without advice.

tips.title: Contract workers have statutory protections — check the principal employer and the contractor
tips.cost: No cost.
tips.inPlainWords: Under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970, covered principal employers must register and contractors must hold a licence. The principal employer can be liable for wages and welfare when the contractor fails. EPF, ESIC and safety duties may also apply. Keep your attendance, wage and contractor details.
tips.benefit: The Contract Labour Act, EPF/ESIC and the OSH Code can create principal-employer liability, which is the key protection.
tips.sources: Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970. <https://labour.gov.in/>; EPFO. <https://www.epfo.gov.in/>; ESIC. <https://esic.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Coverage thresholds and state rules vary. Equal pay for equal work is not automatic in every contract-labour case.
